before.title: Agent swarm: headless specialist agents, conflict-free, token-cheap
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

notes.text: Status was "queued" in _claude/builds/profiles/breakroom/orchestrator.json (not an orchestrator@1 status; the orchestrator always read it as pending).

steps.text: FIRST: preview page rendering all 4 card designs with sample agents in the current theme; ping Brett to pick the default
Agent roster + agent@1 skills: Kotlin/Compose, React UI, Python server, plugin manifests, assets/themes, tests, docs, merge-fixer; each skill file under one page
Card designer (edit layout/fields/logo, Save as new) + default picker + per-agent override + editable identity fields
agent-card@1 asset type + 4 branded starter card assets (logo slot, theme tokens only), web + Android renderers
Job planner: split a build into jobs, pick agent + cheapest capable model, file leases, overlap sequencing

after.title: Agent swarm: headless specialist agents, conflict-free, token-cheap
after.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

before.title: Agent voice plugin: agents speak + per-agent narrator console, live status light, Assistant mic
before.detail: Brett Oct 29 2026: Build a plugin giving agents the ability to speak, with a full powerful per-agent configuration console and every bell and whistle a narrator should have. When a voice agent is selected a live status icon lights up on the main application and the Assistant window. A microphone in the Assistant window: when selected, a tooltip notes the selected agent's name is missing permission — unless the plugin isn't installed, then it says so with links to install, or a hook to install it with the agent. Powerful microphone configuration with integrated features and settings that never conflict with other listening (AmberX notes/dictation and voice/wake). Voices: both device + cloud, with hooks to its settings in multiple places. Profile: Refactor. Model: Opus (web console plugin + AmberX native seam).

notes.text: s1-s8 done on feat/agent-voice; PR create held on axHub (approval 45ca37d6). s9 left: CI + merge approval.

steps.text: Contract + pure core (agent-voice@1): per-agent voice profiles, narration engine (pronunciation dictionary, pauses, emphasis, number/code/URL reading modes, chunking, markdown stripping), presets; self-test
Server: profiles store (0600 in dataDir), cloud TTS proxy (OpenAI, ElevenLabs) with keys server-side, voice lists, audio cache, test.py
Speech engines: device (AmberX native TTS / Web Speech) + cloud audio player, queue, pause/resume/skip/stop, barge-in
Mic broker + mic settings that never conflict with AmberX hands-free wake, dictation and notes listening
Per-agent configuration console (agents list, voice picker + test, narrator controls, permissions, pronunciation, presets, import/export)

Assistant integration: ai-assistant slots + events, fallback mic with 'not installed' tooltip + install links / install-with-agent hook, plugin mic with missing-permission tooltip, live light in the title bar, auto-speak replies
Banner live status light + settings hooks in app menu, context menu, assistant, banner
AmberX native: speak with voice/rate/pitch/volume, voice list, speaking events, hands-free yields while speaking
Lifecycle (install/uninstall/hooks), docs, checks, PR + merge approval

before.title: UI Review: one plugin where Brett approves every UI a build makes (Design packs renamed and widened)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice, driving): rename the Design packs console plugin to UI Review (folder ui-review) and make it one all-in-one UI approval plugin. Every UI a build makes is submitted there for his approval, separated by kind (open registry: Design packs, Whole apps / programs, Screens & pages, Settings interfaces, Dialogs & popups, Menus & toolbars, Banners & cards, Other). Items: title, kind, app, build/branch/PR, desktop + phone shots, notes, status (waiting / approved / changes asked / rejected), his comment, history. Views: tree, collapsible grid, grid with sub-grids, gallery, compare; multi-select + bulk decisions in every view. Builds submit through review.mjs, the plugin API and rebuild-shots --submit; capability ui-review@1. Design-pack picks (MAX 3) migrate. Profile: Angel. Web only.

before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): strip the audio out of his phone screen recordings into an audio file; extraction from a video file only, no live mic, no fallbacks. Then: add a Record screen mode (MediaProjection + playback capture, foreground service, chip, countdown) whose recordings go straight through the extractor. Profile: Angel. Opus, one session.

notes.text: Built on claude/audio-extract (Opus). Web: console plugin audio-extract (targets amberx-droid). Native: AudioExtractPlugin/AudioExtractor/ScreenRecordService. javac-checked locally vs android-35 + Capacitor 8.5.3; APK from CI job amberx. No MP3 (Android has no MP3 encoder); screen-recording folders are SAF grants (no storage permission).

before.title: AmberX Audio Output Recorder -> axHub (no mic)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): AmberX plugin that records all audio the phone outputs while it is on, saved to the server on axHub. One switch + quick-settings tile. Playback capture only, NEVER the microphone. Android 10+; system consent prompt each start and a notification while recording. Calls and opt-out apps (DRM) cannot be captured. 30-minute timestamped chunks, each uploaded to axHub; keep the local file until axHub confirms, queue and retry when offline, small local cap. Built on the capture engine from claude/audio-extract (PR #187).

before.title: Fable rebuild: agent swarm (steps Opus built that were pinned to Fable)
before.detail: Fable suggested, Opus chosen rule: s1-s3, s11, s12, s15 of agent-swarm were pinned to Fable and built on Opus (branch claude/agent-swarm). The Fable build starts by reading and then replacing the Opus version.

notes.text: Oct 31 2026: agent-swarm grew to 19 steps on main (renumbered). Fable-pinned steps built on Opus now: s1 card preview page, s2 roster + skills, s3 card designer, s4 agent-card@1 asset type (framework/core/engines/agent-card-rules.mjs, react/components/AgentCard.tsx, fixture agent-card.json, check-agent-card.mts), s5 job planner, s6 context packer, s14 cards + profiles, s15 group chat, s18 chat settings. The Fable rebuild covers all of them; its agent-card@1 review may keep or replace the Opus contract (Kotlin twin still deferred while Android is on hold).

steps.text: Start: read the Opus version (apps/console-web/plugins/agent-swarm) and its tests; redesign the contracts agent@1, agent-skill@1, swarm-roster@1, swarm-job@1, swarm-report@1 as framework contracts (asset-types / schemas) where they belong
Job planner: model tiers, skill matching, lease overlap and wave sequencing reviewed and replaced where better; keep the planner tests passing or replace them with stronger ones
Context packer + cached shared prefix: measure brief sizes, tighten snippet extraction
Agent cards/profiles: avatars and card layout as assets (everything-is-an-asset rule), not component-drawn
Group chat contract (swarm-state@1 messages, Boss work lines, banter batch)
Vibe engine: scoring, ceiling, tone-down/drop as a pure engine with a fixture
Differences report _claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/agent-swarm.md + LOG.md entry + screenshots

after.title: Molly: one interface for AmberX, axHub and the Dev Console (Opus)
after.detail: Brett, Nov 2 2026: combine AmberX, axHub and the console into one interface but keep them separate apps. Opus version named Molly at molly.amberxai.com; a Fable version comes later in its own build. New app apps/molly (own manifest, baked framework, shared assets) is a shell that shows each app at its own live URL in a kept-alive frame with one banner, one app switcher, one hub sign-in and the look from axHub. Hard rule: AmberX, axHub and the console are not edited and keep running on their own URLs exactly as now; the only allowed outside change is a frame-ancestors header allowing molly.amberxai.com, if needed. No embed marker, no takes, no hiding or merging their menus (same as the Patches rule). No plain axHub hub page, all data on axHub, no storage picker. Patches code is not touched (paused).

steps.text: Project manifest apps/molly/project.manifest.json, add Molly to framework/schemas/shared-assets.json, plan notes
Scaffold apps/molly with axf init (react-ts), baked framework + shared assets, landing screen + settings interface
Shell: app switcher (AmberX / axHub / Console) and one banner, from menu/toolbar/layout assets only
App frames: each app at its own URL, kept alive per tab, deep links #/<app>/<route>, plain URLs (no embed marker)
Framing check: confirm each app lets molly.amberxai.com frame it; if not, add only a frame-ancestors allow header (no app UI change)
One hub sign-in and look from axHub (hubstatus badge red until live), settings on axHub, no storage picker
Checks: check-theme, check-controls, project validate, typecheck/build, shared-assets check, add Molly to CI
Separation test: the three apps' builds and files unchanged (diff limited to apps/molly + config), each still runs alone
Deploy: static image + Coolify app, DNS A record molly.amberxai.com to the VPS, DNS log line
UI Review: desktop + phone shots submitted, PR opened (waits on review)

after.title: xLayout: Molly as one app (one banner, app menu, nav, context menu, toolbars) + IDE panes + plugin toolbars
after.detail: Brett Nov 2 2026 13:46 ET: Molly is whack. Create application menus, navigation menus, context menus, toolbars and a banner that integrate all the apps (AmberX, axHub web, Dev Console): only ONE banner, application menu, navigation menu and context menu render, covering the whole page; the user must not be able to tell it is multiple apps. New plugin xLayout renders it that way. A switch makes it IDE style: draggable, resizable, dockable panes. Plugin toolbars: from the plugin's settings, show/hide up to 3 toolbars and set each default location. A hook in those settings opens a Toolbar designer dialog: pick items from a list of every plugin and screen; each item opens in the main area or a floating window, or (IDE mode on) a pane. Right-clicking any toolbar also has a hook to open the Toolbar designer. IDE mode limits the number of panes and offers ~10 predetermined pane layouts with a preview before applying. Molly-only: standalone, each app stays exactly as it is. Replaces the queued 'Molly: one app' item. Rules: assets/tokens only, framework controls, settings level toolbar, plugin lifecycle, UI Review.

steps.text: xlayout@1 asset type (Fable): chrome-merge model, pane tree, pane limit, 10 layout presets as data, 3 toolbar slots (visible, location), toolbar items + open target (main|floating|pane); asset-types.json, validators, reference engine, fixture

Unified chrome engine (Fable): merge each app's app menu, nav, context menu, toolbars and banner widgets into one namespaced model; guests send chrome as data, host runs picks back (embed@1 takes, Molly host only)
Pane engine (Fable): dock/split/drag/resize tree, pane limit, apply a preset with content kept, open-in-pane routing
xLayout plugin scaffold in Molly: plugin.json, install/uninstall, Settings → Plugins → xLayout sub-tab (level toolbar), IDE mode switch
One banner + application menu + navigation menu + context menu across the whole page in Molly
Guests (AmberX, axHub web, Console) send menus/nav/context/toolbars as data under Molly and hide their own; standalone unchanged
IDE pane host: draggable, resizable, dockable panes; open-in-pane
Layout picker: 10 preset pane layouts, preview before apply, pane limit enforced
Plugin toolbars: up to 3 per plugin/screen, show/hide, default location, in the plugin's settings
Toolbar designer dialog: items from every plugin and screen, open target main/floating/pane; opened from the settings hook and right-click on any toolbar
Tests, check-theme/check-controls, help packs, lifecycle check
UI Review shots (desktop + phone), PR, THREADS

before.title: xLayout: Molly as one app (one banner, app menu, nav, context menu, toolbars) + IDE panes + plugin toolbars
before.detail: Brett Nov 2 2026 13:46 ET: Molly is whack. Create application menus, navigation menus, context menus, toolbars and a banner that integrate all the apps (AmberX, axHub web, Dev Console): only ONE banner, application menu, navigation menu and context menu render, covering the whole page; the user must not be able to tell it is multiple apps. New plugin xLayout renders it that way. A switch makes it IDE style: draggable, resizable, dockable panes. Plugin toolbars: from the plugin's settings, show/hide up to 3 toolbars and set each default location. A hook in those settings opens a Toolbar designer dialog: pick items from a list of every plugin and screen; each item opens in the main area or a floating window, or (IDE mode on) a pane. Right-clicking any toolbar also has a hook to open the Toolbar designer. IDE mode limits the number of panes and offers ~10 predetermined pane layouts with a preview before applying. Molly-only: standalone, each app stays exactly as it is. Replaces the queued 'Molly: one app' item. Rules: assets/tokens only, framework controls, settings level toolbar, plugin lifecycle, UI Review.

notes.text: Brett Nov 2 13:49 ET: the Toolbar designer is its own plugin, not part of xLayout. xLayout calls it through a capability service (e.g. axf.toolbar-designer@1).
Nov 2 21:30 ET: s3 pane engine is covered by Urgent build dock-engine (shared with MD Studio + Theme Editor); s7/s8 build on it. Don't build s3 separately.

before.title: xLayout: Molly as one app (one banner, app menu, nav, context menu, toolbars) + IDE panes + plugin toolbars
before.detail: Brett Nov 2 2026 13:46 ET: Molly is whack. Create application menus, navigation menus, context menus, toolbars and a banner that integrate all the apps (AmberX, axHub web, Dev Console): only ONE banner, application menu, navigation menu and context menu render, covering the whole page; the user must not be able to tell it is multiple apps. New plugin xLayout renders it that way. A switch makes it IDE style: draggable, resizable, dockable panes. Plugin toolbars: from the plugin's settings, show/hide up to 3 toolbars and set each default location. A hook in those settings opens a Toolbar designer dialog: pick items from a list of every plugin and screen; each item opens in the main area or a floating window, or (IDE mode on) a pane. Right-clicking any toolbar also has a hook to open the Toolbar designer. IDE mode limits the number of panes and offers ~10 predetermined pane layouts with a preview before applying. Molly-only: standalone, each app stays exactly as it is. Replaces the queued 'Molly: one app' item. Rules: assets/tokens only, framework controls, settings level toolbar, plugin lifecycle, UI Review.

notes.text: Brett Nov 2 13:49 ET: the Toolbar designer is its own plugin, not part of xLayout. xLayout calls it through a capability service (e.g. axf.toolbar-designer@1).
Nov 2 21:30 ET: s3 pane engine is covered by Urgent build dock-engine (shared with MD Studio + Theme Editor); s7/s8 build on it. Don't build s3 separately.

s3 (pane engine) covered by dock-engine (Urgent, complete on branch claude/molly-fable): core/engines/dock.ts + DockHost. s1-s2 built on Fable on the same branch (xlayout@1, chrome@1). s4-s12 are the Opus phase: run from this branch after it merges.

Unified chrome engine (Fable): merge each app's app menu, nav, context menu, toolbars and banner widgets into one namespaced model; guests send chrome as data, host runs picks back (embed@1 takes, Molly host only)
Pane engine (Fable): dock/split/drag/resize tree, pane limit, apply a preset with content kept, open-in-pane routing
xLayout plugin scaffold in Molly: plugin.json, install/uninstall, Settings → Plugins → xLayout sub-tab (level toolbar), IDE mode switch
One banner + application menu + navigation menu + context menu across the whole page in Molly

before.title: Fix: switches and tab buttons dead inside interface tabs
before.detail: Brett Oct 27 2026: Appearance switches in console settings and the layout (interface) buttons at the top do nothing. Fix: scoped settings forward every member except get to the shared registry.

before.title: Refactor: everything left to build, one build (Oct 28 2026)
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 28 2026 15:26: "Stop everything from every session right now except the documentation. Put everything left to build into 1 single build in a new session. Send the build to orchestrator and create the matrix then end all other sessions."

One build holding every unfinished step in the Refactor profile (17 source builds, now archived with a note pointing here). Run it in ONE new session; one Fable phase, then one Opus phase (one model switch).

Rules for this build:
- The feature matrix (_claude/builds/profiles/refactor/matrices.json, matrix "refactor-all") is the scope. Kept items are the steps below; skipped items stay in the matrix and are not built. Ticking a skipped item = add it as a step (feature-matrix Apply, once built).
- Carry on from the existing branches and PRs; don't redo finished steps. Open PRs: basic-filter #155 (CI green, merge approval sent), windows-terminal #158, amberx-handsfree #141, enterprise-branding PR #128 + interface-roller PR #129 (stacked; Opus work on opus/enterprise-branding).
- Enterprise-branding's refactor runs first in the Opus phase, so every plugin built after it lands on the refactored console. Every UI in this build is held to framework/spec/DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md, not just the §13 scope.

before.title: Console Home cards: card@1 asset plugins carry, Home detects/shows/hides every card (always rendered), card layouts, cards for every data plugin
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 29 2026: "Design a bunch more cards for the console home screen. If plugins with data or dynamic content don't have a card, design one for them from scratch (you decide what to display and how). Plugins can now carry cards that can be designed in the future SDK and attached to the plugin as assets. Console Home detects all card assets attached to plugins and shows or hides them, but always rendered. The card layout can show or hide all cards detected."

Decisions (cards): profile Angel (new, this is its first build; nothing built in the asking session); Fable contract first, then Opus.
Card designs: one per plugin with data/dynamic content (31 plugins + 5 existing Home cards). No card: _template, basic-filter, plugin-switches, plugins-menu (tools with no data of their own).
Clash check Oct 29: no open build touches Home or cards (refactor profile all complete; main-framework pending items unrelated).

steps.text: card@1 asset type in framework/schemas/asset-types.json (+ axf schemas): id, owner (plugin id or "console"), title, icon, kind (stat | list | meter | chart | feed | status | actions | custom), size (s | m | l | wide | tall), data {service (plugin_services capability), path, refreshSec, live:boolean}, slots (headline, value, sub, rows, sparkline, actions), emptyState, actions (ids run through the action engine), level (Simple/Basic/Developer/Administrator), minRole (UAC), defaultVisible, order, category. Open registry: unknown kinds render the custom slot, never fail.

plugin@1 gets `cards: ["cards/<id>.json", …]` (card assets ship inside the plugin folder, so plugin-lifecycle@1 removes them on uninstall); plugin-inventory@1 engine lists each plugin's cards (framework/core/engines/plugins.ts + server/engine.py twin) so anything can detect them; future card SDK attaches cards to a plugin by writing this list.

home-cards@1 engine (TS reference, framework/core/engines/cards.ts): collects every card from enabled plugins + console-owned cards, applies saved visibility/order/size, level and role; hidden cards stay in the output with `hidden: true` so Home ALWAYS renders (mounts) every card and only hides it (instant show, data kept warm). Fixture spec/fixtures/home-cards.json; Kotlin twin recorded as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).

card-layout@1 asset type: columns per window class (compact/medium/expanded), gap + density tokens, grouping (none | plugin | category), "show all / hide all" default, sort (manual | category | plugin). 3 starter layouts: grid-auto, two-column-dashboard, compact-list. Hot-swap via runtime.swap('card-layout', id); tokens only (THEMING.md).

Placeholders for the future card SDK: `axf.cards@1` capability service (list/register/unregister cards at runtime), extension point `home.cards`, typed NotImplemented card designer entry, so a designer plugin can later author card assets and attach them to any plugin without kernel changes.

Home renders from the home-cards engine. The 5 cards already there become console-owned card assets: Plan summary, Build summary, Coverage, Project, Recent installs & imports. Same look at the default theme.

Card layout toolbar on Home (hideable): Show all · Hide all · layout picker (card-layout assets) · group by · a Cards checklist popover with one switch per detected card. Right-click a card: Hide card · Card size · Open plugin · Plugin settings. Drag to reorder. Saved per user in settings (synced through axHub like the rest).
Settings → Home cards tab (with the level toolbar rule): every detected card grouped by plugin, switch + size + order, layout default; a card whose plugin is disabled shows greyed "plugin off".

before.title: AmberX Audio Output Recorder -> axHub (no mic)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): AmberX plugin that records all audio the phone outputs while it is on, saved to the server on axHub. One switch + quick-settings tile. Playback capture only, NEVER the microphone. Android 10+; system consent prompt each start and a notification while recording. Calls and opt-out apps (DRM) cannot be captured. 30-minute timestamped chunks, each uploaded to axHub; keep the local file until axHub confirms, queue and retry when offline, small local cap. Built on the capture engine from claude/audio-extract (PR #187).

before.title: Agent swarm: headless specialist agents, conflict-free, token-cheap
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

before.title: xLayout: Molly as one app (one banner, app menu, nav, context menu, toolbars) + IDE panes + plugin toolbars
before.detail: Brett Nov 2 2026 13:46 ET: Molly is whack. Create application menus, navigation menus, context menus, toolbars and a banner that integrate all the apps (AmberX, axHub web, Dev Console): only ONE banner, application menu, navigation menu and context menu render, covering the whole page; the user must not be able to tell it is multiple apps. New plugin xLayout renders it that way. A switch makes it IDE style: draggable, resizable, dockable panes. Plugin toolbars: from the plugin's settings, show/hide up to 3 toolbars and set each default location. A hook in those settings opens a Toolbar designer dialog: pick items from a list of every plugin and screen; each item opens in the main area or a floating window, or (IDE mode on) a pane. Right-clicking any toolbar also has a hook to open the Toolbar designer. IDE mode limits the number of panes and offers ~10 predetermined pane layouts with a preview before applying. Molly-only: standalone, each app stays exactly as it is. Replaces the queued 'Molly: one app' item. Rules: assets/tokens only, framework controls, settings level toolbar, plugin lifecycle, UI Review.

steps.text: Live status writes to main: store writes committed to main at once as status-only commits (git plumbing on origin/main, bounded rebase-retry, never force), per-build newer-wins merge, journal union

Banners + THREADS follow the store: every live status change pushes the banner update and appends a THREADS.md line
Session-start rule: sessions run the reconciler and read the live store first, never the main export alone

before.title: Tools plugin: the Tools section as its own plugin, with a Tools tab in Patches web
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 22 2026: the Tools section is a plugin of its own, and Claude handoff depends on it.

- New plugin `tools` (plugin@1 + lifecycle): it owns the Tools nav section and the top-level `tools` application menu that tool plugins add to; it provides a capability service (e.g. `axf.tools@1`) that tool plugins require.
- Claude handoff (and any later tool plugin) declares it as a dependency (`requires`) and adds its entries through it instead of creating the section itself.
- For Patches: the Tools plugin adds a **Tools** tab to Patches web's app tab group (next to Console / Pilot / axHub). Patches itself runs the Tools page; it is not the console page in a frame.
- Patches web only for now (Android later).

before.detail: Brett Nov 2 2026 21:30 ET: powerful MD file browser/editor. Opens multiple md files in a tab group with floating, dockable, resizable tabs. A column lists every md file in collapsible categories by scope: Project, Claude, Repo; an edit switch makes a file editable. If a file references other files the chain shows as branches; clicking a referenced name splits the viewing area (setting: vertical or horizontal). Right-click any file in the column: open in horizontal or vertical split. A split section can be undocked, floated, and dropped as a tab in any tab header or into a split (the split shows while hovering). Toolbar with 3 views plus a 4th IDE-style view, each changing how everything renders. Drag snippets into files; wizards that create Claude md files (CLAUDE.md, rules, persona, threads, skills...), categorized by what they do and by scope (project, Claude, repo). Builds on dock-engine.

before.title: Orchestrator live sync: every step reaches main at once
before.detail: Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): every completed step, however small, must reach the orchestrator and show on main immediately, so banners and THREADS follow every step. Store writes go live to main as status-only commits; branch + PR auto-link; reconciler for open PRs and claude/* branches; banners + THREADS follow the store; session-start rule; backfill.

steps.text: Live status writes to main: store writes committed to main at once as status-only commits (git plumbing on origin/main, bounded rebase-retry, never force), per-build newer-wins merge, journal union
Branch + PR auto-link: build branch/pr fields set and written live; built-awaiting-merge when all steps done but the PR is open, complete when merged
Reconciler: scan open PRs and claude/* branches, match to builds, fill branch/pr, mark finished work, flag orphans (report + banner alert), on session start and a timer
Banners + THREADS follow the store: every live status change pushes the banner update and appends a THREADS.md line
Session-start rule: sessions run the reconciler and read the live store first, never the main export alone
Backfill: dock-engine, token-control, urgent-builds, theme-editor; reconciler across angel, big-dog, breakroom, refactor, urgent

before.title: AmberX: hands-free listening on screen + in background, ActiveX-style detection overlay (level graph, dB, quick settings)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 27 2026 (claude.ai): 'It only detects words when I press speak' in AmberX (apps/amberx-droid). Cause: the native wake listener runs only while 'Watch axHub in the background' is on (default off) and pauses while the app is on screen. Fix: hands-free listening is its own setting (default on), works on screen and in the background, independent of axHub monitoring; optional always-armed (no wake phrase). Plus a detection overlay like ActiveX: floating draggable window over other apps with a moving audio-level line graph, decibel number, what was heard, and quick settings (listening on/off, always armed, hide). Colours from the app's theme tokens. Profile refactor, Opus (Brett's pick). Android exception: AmberX shell is allowed (rule Oct 25).

steps.text: Notes core: lists tree (categories, sub-lists, Inbox, Plugins root auto-filled with a list per plugin), notes/todos/tasks model, move/rename/merge, intent schema + validator, local voice-intent parser

Tasks + Todo page: status, priority, due, checklist, subtasks; tabs Today / Upcoming / All / Done; grid and tree views

Brett, Oct 28 2026 15:26: "Stop everything from every session right now except the documentation. Put everything left to build into 1 single build in a new session. Send the build to orchestrator and create the matrix then end all other sessions."

One build holding every unfinished step in the Refactor profile (17 source builds, now archived with a note pointing here). Run it in ONE new session; one Fable phase, then one Opus phase (one model switch).

Rules for this build:
- The feature matrix (_claude/builds/profiles/refactor/matrices.json, matrix "refactor-all") is the scope. Kept items are the steps below; skipped items stay in the matrix and are not built. Ticking a skipped item = add it as a step (feature-matrix Apply, once built).
- Carry on from the existing branches and PRs; don't redo finished steps. Open PRs: basic-filter #155 (CI green, merge approval sent), windows-terminal #158, amberx-handsfree #141, enterprise-branding PR #128 + interface-roller PR #129 (stacked; Opus work on opus/enterprise-branding).
- Enterprise-branding's refactor runs first in the Opus phase, so every plugin built after it lands on the refactored console. Every UI in this build is held to framework/spec/DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md, not just the §13 scope.
- Patches stays paused; skip Patches in every re-bake. Android only in apps/amberx-droid.
- Kept: 30 h 50 min (11 h 45 min Fable). Skipped by default: 10 h 25 min.

before.title: Agent swarm: headless specialist agents, conflict-free, token-cheap
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

before.detail: Brett Nov 2 2026 13:46 ET: Molly is whack. Create application menus, navigation menus, context menus, toolbars and a banner that integrate all the apps (AmberX, axHub web, Dev Console): only ONE banner, application menu, navigation menu and context menu render, covering the whole page; the user must not be able to tell it is multiple apps. New plugin xLayout renders it that way. A switch makes it IDE style: draggable, resizable, dockable panes. Plugin toolbars: from the plugin's settings, show/hide up to 3 toolbars and set each default location. A hook in those settings opens a Toolbar designer dialog: pick items from a list of every plugin and screen; each item opens in the main area or a floating window, or (IDE mode on) a pane. Right-clicking any toolbar also has a hook to open the Toolbar designer. IDE mode limits the number of panes and offers ~10 predetermined pane layouts with a preview before applying. Molly-only: standalone, each app stays exactly as it is. Replaces the queued 'Molly: one app' item. Rules: assets/tokens only, framework controls, settings level toolbar, plugin lifecycle, UI Review.

before.detail:
Brett, Oct 22 2026: the Tools section is a plugin of its own, and Claude handoff depends on it.

- Patches web only for now (Android later).

before.title: Build Pilot plugin contract (Fable rebuild)
before.detail: Rebuild the pilot-plugin@1 contract in MossesX/Build-Pilot (src/pilot/contract.ts + stacks.ts): stack-scoped plugins (one stack, several, or * for all), steps, build patches, compose/merge/conflict rules, checks, and the pilot-project@1 format, so it ports cleanly to the Android version of Build Pilot and to every future stack. The Opus version was built Oct 19 2026; keep its tests (tests/contract.test.ts) passing or replace them with stricter ones, and keep the five Android/all-stack plugins working.

steps.text: Read first (Build-Pilot repo must be attached): `src/pilot/contract.ts`, `stacks.ts`, `tests/contract.test.ts`, the five Android/all-stack plugins, `server/assembly.py`. Write `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/build-pilot-contract.md` skeleton: what the Opus contract has, what the rebuild changes (stack scoping rules, step model, patch/compose/conflict rules, checks, pilot-project@1), what stays.

Types: rewrite `pilot-plugin@1` manifest + `PilotStep`, `BuildPatch`, `ComposeResult`, `PilotProject` (`pilot-project@1`) as a pure, port-neutral module `src/pilot/contract/types.ts` with no DOM/React imports; JSON Schema generated for both documents (`schemas/`). Old manifests still parse (versioned `$axf`).

Stack scoping: `servesStack(plugin, stack)` for one / several / `*`, stack registry open (`stacks.ts` reads `stacks.json`), `pluginsFor(stack)` ordered by `order` then id; unit tests incl. unknown stack refused.

Compose + merge: `compose(request, contributions)` merges patches in plugin order with the conflict rules (same key from two plugins → conflict unless `merge: append|deep|last`), reports every conflict with both sources; deterministic output snapshot test.

Checks: `check(project)` runs plugin `check()` hooks + built-in checks (manifest valid, slots pick assets that will ship — reuse AXF `checkSlotPicks` through the console API shape —, hidden slots hideable, build options known from `GET /api/build-options`); results typed `PilotCheck` with severity + fix.

Fixtures for every port: `tests/fixtures/pilot-contract.json` generated from the TS reference (servesStack, pluginsFor, compose incl. conflicts, check) so the Kotlin port (`console-android-native-tabs` step 1) and Python replay it; `tests/contract.test.ts` replays it too (stricter than the Opus tests).
Python mirror: `server/pilot_contract.py` replaying the fixture (used by `assembly.py`'s gate so the server never trusts the browser's compose); `server/test_server.py` kept passing.

Migrate the five plugins (`android-app`, `look`, `build-options`, `feature-manager`, `custom-features`) to the new types; a `pilot-project@1` loader with migration from the Opus format; the designer still builds an APK end to end (dispatch `pilot-apk.yml` once).

Docs + close: plugin author guide section in Build-Pilot README, differences report finished, LOG.md line in AmberX-AXF, pending complete; AXF side: note in CLAUDE.md Status (Build Pilot hooks) if the console API shape changed (it should not).

before.title: Console Android app: native Pilot + axHub tabs (no web content)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 20 2026: option B — Build Pilot and the axHub admin pages running natively in the Android console app (Compose), no web views. This is the Android version of Build Pilot (roadmap) plus a native hub admin client, built as small Fable steps that each stand alone. Depends on the pending `axhub-agent-host` for sessions and on axHub's admin API (its step 4). Work on it a little at a time: every sub prompt ships something usable.

notes.text: ON HOLD (Brett, Oct 21 2026): don't build the console or Build Pilot Android apps any more — Brett will finish them himself later. Never start this item (or any step of it) unless he says so.

steps.text: 1a. Pilot contract on Kotlin, types: `axf-pilot-core` pure-Kotlin module (`framework/android/axf-pilot-core`) with `PilotPluginManifest`, `PilotStep`, `BuildPatch`, `BuildRequest` (incl. `hidden`/`assets`) data classes mirroring Build-Pilot's `src/pilot/contract.ts` after its Fable rebuild (`build-pilot-contract`).
1b. Manifest checks + `servesStack`/`pluginsFor` in Kotlin, replaying `spec/fixtures/pilot-contract.json` (copied from Build-Pilot's generated fixture into `framework/spec/fixtures/`).
1c. `compose` merge + conflict rules in Kotlin, same fixture section; `PilotContractConformanceTest` in CI (`:axf-pilot-core:test`).

1d. Fixture sharing: a script in Build-Pilot (`npm run fixtures:export`) writes the fixture; AmberX-AXF CI fails if the copied fixture's hash differs from the one Build-Pilot publishes in its README (manual sync, documented).

2a. Pilot API client, models: Kotlin data classes for `/api/projects`, `/api/catalog`, `/assemble`, `/build`, `/apk`, `/metering/me` responses mirroring `server/main.py`; kotlinx.serialization, lenient unknown keys.
2b. Pilot API client, transport: `PilotClient` over axf-network with the token from SecureStore and the hub-admin sign-in reused (cookie provider), timeouts, no redirects, typed errors.
2c. Pilot API client, tests: MockWebServer test per route (happy path, 401, 5xx, malformed JSON), token never logged; CI job line.

3a. Android plugin face: define the `android/` part of `pilot-plugin@1` (a Compose `steps` composable entry + the same `contribute`/`check` shape) as Kotlin interfaces in `axf-pilot-core`; manifest field `android: { module }`.

3b. Loader: reads bundled plugin manifests from assets, instantiates Android parts by registered factory (open registry), lists web-only plugins separately; unit test with two fake plugins (one Android, one web-only).
4a. Pilot Home screen: stacks + projects list from `PilotClient`, New project button, error/empty states from theme tokens.
4b. Designer shell: steps from the loaded plugins in order, step navigation, autosave through the API (debounced), unsaved marker.
4c. Build step, part 1: review (composed request summary) + assemble with the agent (calls `/assemble`, shows ops, approve/deny).
4d. Build step, part 2: build + validate (`/build`, `/validate`), history list, retry; generic UI only.
5a. `android-app` plugin Android part: App setup form (name, id, package) with validation parity to the web plugin.
5b. `android-app` boilerplate browser: list from the catalog with screenshots (`GET /api/boilerplates/<id>/screenshots/<file>` through the console), pick one.
5c. `look` plugin Android part: slot picks per type from `framework-assets` (engine-rpc through the console), preview chips.
5d. `build-options` plugin Android part: switches from `GET /api/build-options`, defaults off, descriptions.
5e. `feature-manager` Android part, 1: FeatureList rows (catalog features, grouped), search, selected set.
5f. `feature-manager` Android part, 2: Chrome section (banner/toolbar entries) + Customize/Build now actions wired to the designers (step 6) and the Build step.
5g. `custom-features` Android part: metered Claude request form, usage from `/metering/me`, result list; refused when no key with a clear note.

6a. Banner designer on Android: builds the same asset@1 `banner` document as `src/pilot/designers.tsx` (surface, logo, divider, attach list); widget picker from the engine's app defaults (`typeLabels`/`typeIcons` via the console API).
6b. Toolbar designer on Android: items + widgets start/end + density/surface/collapsible, same asset@1 output; unit test that both designers emit documents that pass the Kotlin validator.

7a. Live preview, frame: a floating phone-frame composable (window via `windows/` engine) rendering the composed request's theme through the Kotlin theme engine; shrink to a pill, drag (same as the web `ScreenMock` behaviour).
7b. Live preview, content: nav/toolbar/banner from the picked assets, screens as placeholders with the boilerplate's screen kinds; updates on every designer change (debounced).
8. APK builds from the phone: Build APK → poll `/apk` → download via `DownloadManager` → install prompt; progress widget bound to a counter (`counter`/`progress` widget kinds).
9a. axHub admin client, models: Kotlin data classes for the hub's step-4 admin API (services, jobs, approvals, audit, users, projects) from its OpenAPI/JSON shapes; lenient parsing.
9b. axHub admin client, transport + tests: `HubAdminClient` over axf-network sharing the AXHub app's session (cookie jar), CSRF header handling, no redirects; MockWebServer tests per route.
9c. Approvals list screen native (replaces the web view the AXHub app uses today): list, filters, pull to refresh.
9d. Single approval screen: details, Approve/Deny through the API with the hub's CSRF rules, PIN prompt when the hub asks, result toast; one-tap link rule honoured from notifications.
10a. Services: list/describe/call with a JSON args editor, destructive confirm card (same rule as lib-mcp's gate).
10b. Jobs: list, detail with progress, cancel.
10c. Audit log viewer: paged list, filter by user/tool, detail sheet.
10d. Vault names: list of names only, set/rotate (write-only; values never shown).
10e. Users + permissions: list, per-user permission switches (`console.*`, `agents.*`, `apps.download`), add user (temporary password flow as the hub does).
10f. Projects tree browser over `axhub.memory_*` (read + edit text files with approval), Apps page (download APKs through `DownloadManager`).
11a. Native tab bar in slot `app.frame.top` (from `console-android-app-tabs` step 1) switching Console / Pilot (native) / axHub (native), each with its own back stack (`NavHost` per tab).
11b. Tab choice shared with the web console through the `app-tabs.*` settings keys (settings-from-axHub when it lands); unit test of the mapping.
12a. Tests: fake-server tests for both clients, Compose tests per screen group (Home/Designer/Build, plugin parts, designers, approvals, services), CI job lines.

12b. Report: rebuild log line, differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/console-android-native-tabs.md`, push `fable/console-android-native-tabs` for `rebuild-shots.yml` screenshots; pending complete.
