before.title: Patches: Android wrapper app (Console + Pilot + axHub tabs) + embed@1
before.detail: Brett, Oct 21 2026 (voice): take the Console / Pilot / axHub tab group out of the Dev Console so Console, Build Pilot and axHub are each their own app again, and make a new app, Patches, that is just one banner + a tab group showing the three apps in tabs; when an app runs inside Patches its own banner is hidden and Patches shows the one banner. Android first (Android hold lifted for Patches, Oct 21; web Patches later). Design Brett chose: native Android shell, web tabs — the Dev Console (console.amberxai.com), Build Pilot (pilot.amberxai.com) and axHub each load in an origin-locked WebView kept alive across tab switches; Build Pilot has no Android app yet, so its tab is the web app. The framework gains embed@1 (cross-port): a host marks the pages it embeds and the embedded app hides the chrome the host shows (its banner by default) over the user's own choice, which stays saved for standalone runs. Model: Fable (changes how GUIs work across apps). Built on Opus-free Fable session Oct 21 2026 in branch fable/patches-wrapper.

notes.text: Hub copy of this list (axhub.memory_* project amberx-axf, data area) held only 10 items on Oct 21 2026 while the repo snapshot held 20 — check `claude-sync status` on the VPS before trusting either; this item was added to the repo snapshot by the Fable build session.

Built Oct 21 2026 on Fable: branch fable/patches-wrapper, PR #5; Android CI green (kernel tests incl. EmbedConformanceTest, lib-hub, patches-debug.apk 20.6 MB). Report _claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/patches-wrapper.md.

steps.text: 1a. Framework embed@1 (web reference): `core/engines/embed.ts` — the marker a host app puts on the pages it embeds (query `?axf-embed=<host>[&axf-embed-hide=…]`, user agent `AXF-Embed/<host>[/<types>]`), host id rules, hidden-chrome cleaning (hideable types only, default banner, `none`), host helpers `userAgentSuffix` / `embedUrl`; fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.

1b. Hide engine forced layer + runtime (web): `hiddenSlots(overrides, defaults, forced)`; `AxfRuntime.embedded` (detected from the page or passed), `embedHiddenSlots`, `slotHiddenByHost`, `setSlotHidden` refuses host-shown chrome with a toast and never writes an override; `AppShell` marks `.fx-frame[data-axf-embed]`; lib-settings greys the slot picker out ("Shown by <host>"); `spec/check-embed.mts` in CI.

1c. Kotlin twins: `EmbedEngine` (same fixture), `HideEngine.hiddenSlots(…, forced)`, `AxfRuntime(embedded = …)` + `slotHiddenByHost`, Compose settings chips greyed; `EmbedConformanceTest` + the hide fixture's forced cases in `ConformanceTest`.

2. Dev Console: remove the App tabs plugin cleanly (`uninstall.mjs --all`, lifecycle check clean), strip its doc lines, keep the `app.frame.top` / `app.frame.cover` slots for other plugins; the console stands alone with its own banner.

3a. Patches app scaffold: `axf init apps/patches` (android-compose, developer app: look + settings from axHub, hub library), app id `patches`, package `ai.amberx.axf.patches`, project manifest (repo `MossesX/patches` reserved), own layout asset `patches-tabs` (top tabs, no menubar/toolbar/status, full width), nav asset `patches-tabs` with the three tabs, manifest hides toolbar/app-menu.

3b. lib-hub `WebAppView`: a full web-app WebView (JavaScript + DOM storage on, cache allowed, origin allowlist with the hub origin for the sign-in wall, no file/content access, no mixed content, downloads to the hub app catalog handler), user agent suffix from `EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix("patches")`, `WebAppHolder` that keeps one WebView per tab alive across tab switches (reparented, never destroyed until the activity goes), back button = page history.

3c. Patches views: three routes (console / pilot / axhub) each rendering the holder's WebView for that tab; the Patches banner (logo, day/night switch, clock, settings button) is the one banner; hub sign-in via the developer-app waiting screen (shared cookie store = one session for every tab); Settings → Patches group: hub address, each tab's URL, reload tab, open in the phone's browser.

4. Wiring: CI (`android.yml` builds every app `app-bundle.mjs list --android` finds → `patches-debug.apk` + app catalog entry), `project.manifest.json` validated (`axf project validate --all`), `framework/catalog` + tracker, CLAUDE.md status, rules note (Android hold exception for Patches), PORTING.md, decisions.md.

5. Proof: web checks (`check-embed`, `check-widgets`, `check-appearance`, `check-app-menu`, `check-hub`, `axf validate --framework`, console typecheck), before/after web screenshots (console with and without the tab group; console embedded = no banner), push `fable/patches-wrapper` (Android shots by `rebuild-shots.yml`), differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/patches-wrapper.md`, LOG.md line, change-log result.

before.title: Patches manages the plugins of the apps it hosts (Opus)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 22 2026: when Patches loads developer apps in tabs, Patches owns all plugins. New embed@1 take `plugins`: inside such a host an app loads only the plugins Patches has installed and enabled for it (its own on/off switches don't apply), and its plugin hooks (Settings → Plugins, Plugin Manager, plugin switches, plugin menu entries) are greyed out with "Plugins are managed in Patches". The app reports the plugins it has (`plugins` message); Patches compares with its own list, tries to install the missing ones by itself, and shows a Systems check entry with Auto fix while any are missing. Web first (patches-web + console); Patches Android and Kotlin twin deferred.

notes.text: Built Oct 22 2026 on Opus, branch claude/project-thread-eew3jm. Not screenshot-verified (the apps wait for axHub in the build sandbox).

steps.text: Framework: embed@1 take `plugins` (lock mode: hooks greyed with a note, not dropped) + messages `plugins` (guest → host report) and `plugins-enabled` (host → guest); fixture cases + check-embed.mts.

Console: inside a host that takes plugins, load only the plugins the host enabled; report its plugins; plugin-manager + plugin-switches show the note.
Patches web server: plugin store per app (/data/plugins.json), routes GET /api/plugins, POST install/enable; tests.
Patches web UI: compare reports, auto install, Systems check banner entry with Auto fix, Settings → Patches → Plugins switches; tabs take `plugins`.
Docs, PORTING.md deferral, CLAUDE.md status, decisions, tests green.

- New plugin `tools` (plugin@1 + lifecycle): it owns the Tools nav section and the top-level `tools` application menu that tool plugins add to; it provides a capability service (e.g. `axf.tools@1`) that tool plugins require.
- Claude handoff (and any later tool plugin) declares it as a dependency (`requires`) and adds its entries through it instead of creating the section itself.
- For Patches: the Tools plugin adds a **Tools** tab to Patches web's app tab group (next to Console / Pilot / axHub). Patches itself runs the Tools page; it is not the console page in a frame.
- Patches web only for now (Android later).

before.title: Console Android app: Pilot + axHub tabs (web views, everything in the app)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 20 2026: the Android console app needs Pilot and axHub tabs like the web console's App tabs plugin. Option A: every tab runs inside the app — Build Pilot (pilot.amberxai.com) and axHub (axhub.amberxai.com, Apps page + approvals) in locked-down in-app web views; nothing ever opens the phone's browser. Fable (the Compose AppShell gains the shared page slots the web shell has). Broken into small builds (sub prompts) so it can be worked on a little at a time; each sub prompt stands alone and leaves the app building.

notes.text: ON HOLD (Brett, Oct 21 2026): don't build the console or Build Pilot Android apps any more — Brett will finish them himself later. Never start this item (or any step of it) unless he says so.

steps.text: 1a. Compose page slots, kernel side: add `ExtensionPoints.PAGE_SLOTS` (`axf.page-slots`, contribution {slot: "app.frame.top" | "app.frame.cover", order, content key}) in `axf-kernel/module/Extensions.kt`, same slot names as `framework/react/components/Slots.tsx`; unit test that contributions order like the web `installLibraries` does.

1b. Compose page slots, UI side: `axf-ui/.../Slots.kt` with `AxfSlot(name)` reading the registry and `AppShell` rendering `app.frame.top` above the banner and `app.frame.cover` over the shell (same positions as the web `AppShell.tsx`); Android console showcase contributes a debug label into each to prove it; compiles in CI.

2a. `lib-apptabs` module skeleton: `framework/android/lib-apptabs` (id `ai.amberx.axf.apptabs`, `settings.gradle.kts` entry, `AppTabsModule` registering a settings group "App tabs" with the same keys as the web plugin `app-tabs.tabs|custom|active`); `:lib-apptabs:testDebugUnitTest` job with one test (keys match the web plugin's constants read from a shared JSON resource).

2b. Tab bar composable `AxfAppTabBar` in slot `app.frame.top`: reads the tab list + active id from settings, console tab = the app itself, action `app-tabs.show:<id>` registered; tapping switches the active setting; no content yet.

2c. Settings sync note: the module reads/writes only through `SettingsRegistry` so settings-from-axHub (decision Oct 20) applies once that lands; add the keys to `framework/android/lib-settings`'s shared-key list; unit test round-trip of `app-tabs.custom` JSON.

3a. Built-in tab list: Console (self), Pilot `https://pilot.amberxai.com`, axHub `https://axhub.amberxai.com/apps`, Demo, as a Kotlin list mirroring the web plugin's built-ins; icons from `axf-ui/icons`.

3b. Manifest tabs: project manifests built on/for AXF with `deploy.url`, read from a bundled `catalog/projects.json` (generated by `sync-data.mjs` into the Android console assets), appended to the list; unit test with a fixture catalog.

4a. `AxfWebTab` web view composable, locked down: allowed hosts only (own domains from manifest/settings), refuse other links with a toast (never the outside browser), JavaScript on, file access off, popups off, geolocation off, mixed content blocked; unit test of the allow rule (pure function `hostAllowed`).

4b. `AxfWebTab` state: one WebView per tab, lazily created, retained across recompositions (`remember` + `AndroidView` holder keyed by tab id), `FLAG_SECURE` honoured from the activity; manual check on the emulator that switching tabs keeps scroll position.

5a. Hub session cookies: `CookieManager` scoped to the app, `android:allowBackup` rules + `dataExtractionRules` exclude the WebView data; sign-in happens on the hub's own login page inside the tab (no JS injection, no off-hub navigation).

5b. Sign-out: a "Sign out of hub" setting clears cookies for every tab and reloads them; the console tab's own token stays in the SecureStore (untouched); unit test that sign-out does not clear SecureStore keys.
6. Downloads: only axHub Apps page APK links, handed to `DownloadManager` with the hub cookie (as `apps/axhub-android` does); everything else refused with a toast; unit test of the link rule.
7a. Cover slot: active non-console tab fills `app.frame.cover` below the bar; back button goes back inside the web view first, then returns to the Console tab (`BackHandler`).
7b. Loading + errors: pull-to-refresh, a "Loading…" bar, a plain error card (offline, 4xx/5xx, refused frame) with Retry, all from theme tokens; emulator check.
8a. Settings → Plugins → App tabs: pick tabs (switch per built-in), order (up/down), reset; `SettingsGroup`/`SettingSpec` with parent = Plugins.
8b. Custom tabs: add name + https address on an allowed host (validated with `hostAllowed`), remove; stored in `app-tabs.custom` with the web plugin's JSON shape.

9. Install: `apps/console` manifest module list + `android-compose` template behind an init option `--app-tabs` (default off; on for the console) in `template.json`, catalog `plugins.json` entry, status.json + tracker (`tracker.mjs --check`).
10a. Tests: `lib-apptabs` unit tests (allowed-host, link rule, settings parity, tab list from manifests) + Compose UI test for bar + cover; CI job line in `android.yml`.

10b. Report: rebuild log line, differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/console-android-app-tabs.md`, push branch `fable/console-android-app-tabs` so `rebuild-shots.yml` captures Android before/after; pending complete.

before.title: Agents + assistant sessions hosted on axHub (one host for every app)
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 20 2026: agents (Build Pilot's pilot-assembler, Mosses and every agent-definition@1 agent) and AI assistant live sessions should run on axHub, not inside each app. Build Pilot, the Dev Console and the phone apps become clients.

- axHub gets an agent + session host: runs turns, owns live-session@1 event logs (sessions survive app restarts and browser closes), per-agent memory, provider keys in axHub's vault, hub permissions for who may use which agent.
- Apps plug in through what the Fable rebuilds left open: the live-session host registry (`axf.live-host@1` / `register_host`, today a typed `axhub` placeholder in the console and Build Pilot), Build Pilot's assembly backend (BP_AGENT=local|console|off → add `axhub`), and the kernel placeholders `axf.agents`, `axhub.agent`.
- axHub never depends on AXF (decision): the host speaks the contracts over its API (AXPP), with an AXF adapter on the AXF side (lib-hub).
- The assembly gate (pilot-assembly@1) stays in Build Pilot: axHub only proposes ops; Build Pilot checks and builds. Manual mode unaffected.
- Needs the axHub repo (MossesX/axHub) attached.

Until then: Build Pilot runs its agent locally (Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026), the console's assistant hosts its own sessions.

steps.text: BRETT attaches MossesX/axHub. Read its session/worker layout, decisions #70–#87 and the AXPP protocol doc; write `_claude/memory/docs/axhub-agent-host.md` design: host API (sessions, turns, events, agents, memory, permissions), where provider keys live (vault, write-only), what the AXF adapter translates. No code.

Protocol contract (AXF side, pure): `framework/core/live-session.ts` gains the wire shape for a remote host (`RemoteHostDescriptor`, event envelope with seq, resume cursor), fixtures in `spec/fixtures/live-session.json` → `remote`; Kotlin `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.live` + Python mirror replay them.

axHub, session store: `sessions` table/collection (id, owner, agent, created, closed, cursor) + append-only event log keyed by seq (file or db per axHub's storage), with replay from a cursor; unit tests.

axHub, turn runner: a worker that runs one turn for a session (provider call through axHub's existing LLM client or a new one using vault keys), streams events into the log, survives the browser going away; one running turn per session; stop/cancel.

axHub, agents: `agent-definition@1` validator ported from `framework/core/agents.ts` (fixture `agents.json` replayed), agent registry per project in `/projects/<name>/_data/agents/`, per-agent memory using the memory engine rules from the contract.

axHub, permissions: who may use which agent / open sessions / write mode, as hub user permissions (`agents.use.<id>`, `sessions.open`, `agents.write`) on the users page, enforced on every host route; admin bypass as elsewhere on the hub.

axHub, host API: `/agents`, `/sessions`, `/sessions/{id}/turns` (POST = run), `/sessions/{id}/events?since=` (SSE + replay), `/sessions/{id}/stop|close`; approvals for destructive tool calls through the hub's approval screen (one-tap link rule). OpenAPI snippet in the design doc.

axHub, provider keys: turns use keys from the vault by name (`llm.<provider>`), never returned; `vault.set` from the console's Keys needed flow already exists — add the names to the systems-check key list on the AXF side later (step 15).

AXF adapter, web: `framework/libs/hub` (lib-hub, first slice exists) gets `AxhubLiveHost implements SessionHost` over the host API with the hub session cookie / token provider; registers through `axf.live-sessions@1.register_host()`; the console's AI assistant picks it when Settings → Assistant → Host = axHub.

AXF adapter, Android: `lib-hub` Kotlin `AxhubLiveHost` over axf-network (SSE reader from `lib-mcp`'s parser), registered in the kernel's live-session host registry; placeholder `axhub.agent` becomes real; written without a compiler, CI unit test with MockWebServer.

Console assistant on the hub host: `ai-assistant` plugin `server/sessions.py` host `axhub` stops being a `PlaceholderHost`: a thin proxy host that forwards to the hub API with the signed-in user's identity; reconnect/replay through the existing `watchReply` fold; `test.py` cases with a fake hub.

Build Pilot: `BP_AGENT=axhub` backend in `server/assembly.py` calling the hub host for the `pilot-assembler` agent; the assembly gate (`pilot-assembly@1`) still checks every op locally; manual mode untouched; `test_server.py` with a fake hub.
Phone apps: the AXHub Android app gets a Sessions tab (list, attach to a live reply, stop) on `lib-hub`'s host client; the Android console's assistant screen (when it exists) uses the same.

Migration: console sessions stored locally can be exported/imported into the hub (`POST /sessions/import` with the event log); one-time "Move my sessions to axHub" button in the assistant settings; no data loss on failure (import is additive).
Systems check: new checks `axhub-agent-host` (host reachable, caller allowed) and the vault key names for providers in the Keys needed list; Auto fix opens the right pages.
Alerts + activity: hub sessions appear in the Activity banner source list (`axf.activity@1`), failed turns raise an alert via the hub → console alerts source `axhub`.
Tests, AXF side: `check-live-session` fixture cases for the remote shape, lib-hub web unit tests (fake SSE), Android unit test, plugin `test.py` additions; CI lines in `android.yml`.
Tests, axHub side: host API tests (permissions, replay from cursor, one turn per session, stop), agent validator fixture replay, vault key never returned.

Deploy: axHub redeploy on Coolify with the worker enabled (env for worker count), console `install-console.sh` passes `AXF_ASSISTANT_HOST=axhub` once the hub answers; BRETT approves the deploy and runs one turn from his phone.
Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/axhub-agent-host.md`, LOG.md, decisions.md (#88+ on the hub side), CLAUDE.md Status in both repos, pending complete.

before.title: Asset templates: 10+ per type + defaults
before.detail: At least 10 editable templates/boilerplates for every asset type the designer covers, plus a default asset per type.

notes.text: Overlaps settings-asset (new `settings` asset type, branch claude/project-thread-55oakl); build with settings-asset-fable.

steps.text: Template index: `framework/assets/templates/index.json` (`asset-templates@1`: id, type, label, tags, file) + loader `listAssetTemplates(type)` in `framework/cli/build-engine.mjs`; engine-rpc `asset-templates`, console `GET /api/asset-templates?type=`. Empty list works end to end.

Validation in CI: `framework/spec/check-asset-templates.mjs` loads every template, runs `validateAsset`, checks unique ids, ≥ 10 per covered type once a type is marked `complete` in the index, and that each type has a `default`. Wire into `android.yml` (node job).

nav-menu ×10: side nav, bottom tabs, rail, grouped sections, icon-only, with badges, two-level, settings-first, admin, minimal. Each a valid `nav-menu` asset in `framework/assets/templates/nav-menu/`.
app-menu ×10 (file/edit/view style menus, single-page apps, tool apps…) + context-menu ×10 (text, list row, card, media, dev, file, link, minimal, with submenus, keyboard hints).
toolbar ×10: editor, media, search-first, compact icons, labelled, split start/end with widgets, status-heavy (counters/progress), collapsible, roomy, minimal.
layout ×10: dashboard, master-detail, sidebar-left/right, bottom-nav phone, kiosk, editor + inspector, chat, settings, full-bleed, three-pane. Each with `data.slots` where it narrows a region.
drawer ×10 (needs `asset-designer` step 7's `drawer` type): left/right, modal/non-modal, wide/narrow, with header, grouped, icon rail, account-first, admin, minimal.

color-theme ×10 light + ×10 dark (pairs): contrast-checked with `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks run from a script; names in one family (`arctic-daylight` style). Each pair shares a `pair` tag.
style-theme ×10: glass, flat, outlined, dense, roomy, rounded, square, hairline, soft, print. Numbers inside ranges known themes use; every opacity token present.

Defaults: `framework/defaults.json` + `framework/app-defaults.json` reviewed so every type has a default template id (new field `templates.default.<type>` read by `axf init` for "start from a template"); `axf init --template-set <id>` option registered in `build-options.json` only if it sets a token, else as an init argument.

Previews: `framework/cli/rebuild-shots.mjs`-style script `framework/cli/template-shots.mjs` renders each template in the demo app headless (phone + desktop) to `framework/assets/templates/<type>/shots/`; `index.json` entries get `shot`. Run once; commit shots ≤ 60 KB each (`framework/cli/shrink-shots.py`).

Android: templates bundled into `axf-assets` as a resource folder so Compose previews (`ComponentGallery.kt`) and the future Android designer read the same files; `AssetTemplates` Kotlin loader + a unit test that every bundled template validates.

Hooks: asset-designer "Start from" and Build Pilot's designers list templates by type (console `GET /api/asset-templates`); asset-browser shows a Templates source. Add the `templates` capability to `app-defaults` engine-rpc.
Close: regenerate fixtures touched (`gen-fixtures.mts`), CI green, report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-templates.md`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan `x.assets.templates` built, pending complete.

before.title: Tools plugin: the Tools section as its own plugin, with a Tools tab in Patches web
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 22 2026: the Tools section is a plugin of its own, and Claude handoff depends on it.

- New plugin `tools` (plugin@1 + lifecycle): it owns the Tools nav section and the top-level `tools` application menu that tool plugins add to; it provides a capability service (e.g. `axf.tools@1`) that tool plugins require.
- Claude handoff (and any later tool plugin) declares it as a dependency (`requires`) and adds its entries through it instead of creating the section itself.
- For Patches: the Tools plugin adds a **Tools** tab to Patches web's app tab group (next to Console / Pilot / axHub). Patches itself runs the Tools page; it is not the console page in a frame.
- Patches web only for now (Android later).

- Patches web only for now (Android later).
